# types of research question


## predictive

can we predict Y based on X?

more based in practical utility.
not so much about understanding, more about utility. 
things get "blackboxed" more - shove lots of info in, get out predictions. 
minimise error. 

e.g. - scottish ambulance services (i think) have an algorithm "SPARRAv4" to predict emergency admissions.  
doesn't say anything about *why* people go to emergency
e.g. people living in lower deprivation areas are more often in AE. 
doesn't mean anything about 


## descriptive

what is the proportion of people with X?

does X coincide with Y?  

- doesn't ask anything about X causing/influencing Y in any way. 
- does chocolate consumption coincide with nobel prize winners?  

"correlation != causation" and all that

## explanatory

most of psych is either explicitly or implicitly in this realm..  


# types of studies

## experiments

- randomly allocate people into groups/conditions  
- put people in both groups. randomly allocate the order.

## Example 1 - Disrupted Nights

```{r}
#| include: false
set.seed(65683728)
eg1sleep <- tibble(
  person = unlist(lapply(1:5, \(x) paste0(LETTERS[x],LETTERS)))[1:80],
  n_disrupted = rep(0:7,e=10),
  psolve = (58 - 1.5 * n_disrupted) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(80,0,7) ~ rep(0:7,e=10)))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)

```

__Question__  

> How does an additional night of interrupted sleep affect problem solving ability?

:::{.fragment}
**Target Quantity**  
What happens to someone's score when we disrupt their sleep for another night?

e.g., person $i$:  

$$
\text{Score}_i^{\text{nights disrupted}=x+1} - \text{Score}_i^{\text{nights disrupted}=x}
$$
:::

## Example 1 - Disrupted Nights (2)
__Question__  

> How does an additional night of interrupted sleep affect problem solving ability?

__Design__  

> We recruit 80 people and randomly allocate them to receiving between 0 to 7 nights of sleep disruption. Upon waking up after their final night of allocated disrupted sleep, participants were given a series of problems to solve. The number of problems and time taken were combined to create an overall score for each participant.

## Example 1 - Disrupted Nights (3)
__Question__  

> How does an additional night of interrupted sleep affect problem solving ability?

__Design__  

> People randomly assigned to 0, 1, 2, ..., 7 nights of sleep disruption. 

__Model__  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{NightsDisrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

::::{.columns .fragment}
:::{.column width="50%"}
__Coefficient__  

- $b_1$ = change in $\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}}$ when $\color{blue}{\text{NightsDisrupted}}$ increases by 1.   

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
fitw = lm(psolve~n_disrupted,eg1sleep)
segsw <- tibble(x1 = 0:6, x2 = x1+1) |> 
  mutate(
    y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    xlp = (x1+x2)/2,
    ylp = (y1+y2)/2
  )
eg1sleep |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=n_disrupted,y=psolve))+
  geom_point(size=3,col="tomato1",alpha=.5)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,se=FALSE,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(x=0,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)
```
:::
::::

## Example 2 - Sleep Interruption 

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(65683728)
xbin = sample(c("Normal","Interrupted"),80,T,prob=c(.6,.4))
eg2sleep <- tibble(
  condition = xbin,
  psolve = (50 + 7.5 * (condition=="Normal")) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(80,0,7) ~ xbin))
)
set.seed(356)
eg2sleep <- slice_sample(eg2sleep, prop=1)
```
__Question__  

> How does having interrupted (vs "normal") sleep affect problem solving ability?

:::{.fragment}
__Target Quantity__  
What happens to someone's score when they are in the "interrupted" group compared to if they were in the "normal" group.  

e.g., person $i$:  

$$
\text{Score}_i^{\text{Condition}='Interrupted'} - \text{Score}_i^{\text{Condition}='Normal'}
$$
:::

## Example 2 - Sleep Interruption (2)

__Question__  

> How does having interrupted (vs "normal") sleep affect problem solving ability?

__Design__  

> We recruit 80 people and randomly allocate them into two groups: we either let them sleep normally ("Normal" group), or we interrupt their sleep every hour ("Interrupted" group). Upon waking, participants were given a series of problems to solve. The number of problems and time taken were combined to create an overall score for each participant.

## Example 2 - Sleep Interruption (3)
__Question__  

> How does having interrupted (vs "normal") sleep affect problem solving ability?

__Design__  

> People randomly assigned to "Normal" or "Interrupted" conditions.  

__Model__  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot (\underbrace{\text{Condition="Interrupted"}}_{\text{1 if 'Interrupted'}\\\text{0 otherwise}})} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

::::{.columns .fragment}
:::{.column width="50%"}
__Coefficient__  

- $b_1$ = change in $\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}}$ when moving from the "Normal" condition to the "Interrupted" condition. 

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
eg2sleep <- eg2sleep |> mutate(
  condition=factor(condition, levels=c("Normal","Interrupted"))
)
fitw = lm(psolve~condition,eg2sleep)
set.seed(3455)
eg2sleep |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=condition, y=psolve))+
  geom_jitter(col = "tomato", size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0\nNormal","1\nInterrupted"))+
  geom_point(x=1,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(x=1,xend=2,y=coef(fitw)[1],yend=coef(fitw)[1],
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF",lwd=2)+
  geom_segment(x=2,xend=2,y=coef(fitw)[1],yend=sum(coef(fitw)),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF",lwd=2)+
  geom_abline(intercept=coef(fitw)[1]-coef(fitw)[2],slope=coef(fitw)[2],
              col="blue",alpha=.3)+
  annotate(geom="label",x=0.9,y=58.5,label="b[0]", parse = TRUE,
           size = 7, col="blue")+
  annotate(geom="label",x=2.05,y=53.75,label="b[1]", parse = TRUE,
           size = 7, col="blue")+
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)
```
:::
::::

## 

- What we're interested in: 
    $\text{Score}_i^{\text{Condition}='Interrupted'} - \text{Score}_i^{\text{Condition}='Normal'}$

- What we're getting: 
    

we want group B to look like what group A _would_ look like _if_ we saw them in group B.  

randomisation!  


## Example 3 - Sleep Quality

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(65683728)
n <- 80
  drink = sample(c("No","Yes"),n,TRUE,prob=c(.4,.6))
  xbin = ifelse(drink=="Yes",
                sample(c("Good", "Bad"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.2, 0.8)),
                sample(c("Good", "Bad"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.8, 0.2)))
  sleep_good <- as.numeric(xbin == "Good")
  drink_yes  <- as.numeric(drink == "Yes")
  
  raw_noise <- rnorm(n, 0, 7)
  noise <- numeric(n)
  noise[drink == "No"]  <- residuals(lm(raw_noise ~ sleep_good, subset = (drink == "No")))
  noise[drink == "Yes"] <- residuals(lm(raw_noise ~ sleep_good, subset = (drink == "Yes")))
  bd <- -8 
  b_scond <- 5 - bd * coef(lm(drink_yes ~ sleep_good))[2]
  eg3sleep <- tibble(
    person = unlist(lapply(26:20, \(x) paste0(LETTERS[x], LETTERS)))[1:80],
    sleep_quality = xbin,
    drank = drink,
    psolve = 55 + b_scond * sleep_good + bd * drink_yes + noise
  ) |> 
    mutate(sleep_quality = factor(sleep_quality, levels = c("Bad", "Good")))

coef(lm(psolve~sleep_quality,eg3sleep[eg3sleep$drank=="Yes",]))

ggplot(eg3sleep, aes(x=sleep_quality,y=psolve,col=drank))+
  geom_jitter(height=0,width=.2)+
  stat_summary(geom="pointrange",position=position_nudge(x=.25))

ggplot(eg3sleep, aes(x=sleep_quality,y=psolve))+
  geom_jitter(height=0,width=.2)+
  stat_summary(geom="pointrange",position=position_nudge(x=.25))  
```

__Question__  

> How does having bad quality sleep affect problem solving ability?  

:::{.fragment}
**Target Quantity**  
What happens to someone's score when they have "Bad" (as opposed to "Good") quality sleep?  

e.g., person $i$:  

$$
\text{Score}_i^{\text{Sleep Quality}=Bad} - \text{Score}_i^{\text{Sleep Quality}=Good}
$$

:::

## Example 3 - Sleep Quality (2)

__Question__  

> How does having bad quality sleep affect problem solving ability?

__Design__  
> We recruit 80 people and ask them to report whether they felt their sleep quality the previous night was "Good" or "Bad". They were given a series of problems to solve. The number of problems and time taken were combined to create an overall score for each participant.  

## Example 3 - Sleep Quality (3)

__Question__  

> How does having bad quality sleep affect problem solving ability?

__Design__  
> Measure people's reported sleep quality ("Good" v "Bad").  

__Model__  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot (\underbrace{\text{SleepQuality="Bad"}}_{\text{1 if 'Bad'}\\\text{0 otherwise}})} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

::::{.columns .fragment}
:::{.column width="50%"}
__Coefficient__    

- $b_1$ = change in $\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}}$ when $\color{blue}{\text{SleepQuality}}$ moves from "Good" to "Bad"  

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
fitw = lm(psolve ~ sleep_quality, eg3sleep)
set.seed(3455)
eg3sleep |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=sleep_quality, y=psolve))+
  geom_jitter(col="tomato",size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0\nGood","1\nBad"))+
  geom_point(x=1,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(x=1,xend=2,y=coef(fitw)[1],yend=coef(fitw)[1],
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF",lwd=2)+
  geom_segment(x=2,xend=2,y=coef(fitw)[1],yend=sum(coef(fitw)),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF",lwd=2)+
  geom_abline(intercept=coef(fitw)[1]-coef(fitw)[2],slope=coef(fitw)[2],
              col="blue",alpha=.3)+
  annotate(geom="label",x=0.95,y=61.5,label="b[0]", parse = TRUE,
           size = 7, col="blue")+
  annotate(geom="label",x=2.05,y=57.5,label="b[1]", parse = TRUE,
           size = 7, col="blue")+
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)
```

:::
::::

## 

- What we're interested in: 
 $\text{Score}_i^{\text{Sleep Quality}=Bad} - \text{Score}_i^{\text{Sleep Quality}=Good}$

- What we're getting: 
    

we want group B to look like what group A _would_ look like _if_ we saw them in group B.  

we're not randomising   

## Example 3 - Sleep Quality (4)

```{r}
#| echo: false
fitw = lm(psolve ~ sleep_quality, eg3sleep)
set.seed(3455)
eg3sleep |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=sleep_quality, y=psolve))+
  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0\nGood","1\nBad"))+
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  stat_summary(geom="pointrange")+
  facet_wrap(~drank)
```
